column1: # coverage-floors.tsv — per-crate line-coverage floors consumed by
# scripts/coverage-gate.sh (--floors; rationale in coverage-gate-plan.md
# section 6).
# Format: <crate-name><TAB><floor-percent>. Lines starting with '#' are
# comments. Crate names must match the gate's lcov fold rows (workspace
# member directory names under crates/). `default` is the fallback floor
# for any measured crate without an explicit row; floor 0 never fails, so
# unlisted crates stay advisory until they gain a row. The TOTAL row is
# printed by the gate but always advisory (never enforced).
# Tier A — pure logic, dense unit pins (floor 80):
#   state-machine / grammar / table code with direct unit pins;
#   dartq-diagnostics measured at 99.15% today (plan section 4).
# Tier B — semantic / engine, resolution-heavy (floor 65):
#   exercised largely via harness and engine integration tests; the
#   unit-visible share is lower.
# Tier C — I/O and CLI boundary (floor 50):
#   real-SDK loading and the process boundary are environment-dependent;
#   only the pure parse/args core is floor-gated.
# Unlisted crates (no floor row => fall back to `default` 0 = advisory):
#   - True empty stubs (1-line lib.rs; auto-dropped by the fold as LF:0
#     rows): dartq-incremental, dartq-cache. Each MUST gain a real floor
#     row in the same PR as its first real implementation.
#   - Real code, no measured baseline yet: dartq-flow, dartq-snapshot,
#     dartq-lints, dartq-ai, dartq-plugin, dartq-schema, dartq-commands,
#     dartq-daemon. They ride `default` until the first full advisory run
#     lands their numbers, then gain tier rows (plan section 7, work
#     item 2) — numbers exist before any floor bites.
#   - Test/tool members, measurement infrastructure not product code:
#     tests/harness (measured as the "harness" row) and tools/corpus-gen;
#     dartq-plugin-host is a Dart package (no Cargo.toml, never measured).
# Ratchet: raise a floor only together with the measured baseline that
# proves it; land advisory first, flip the gate with --enforce once the
# baseline is committed (plan section 6 enforcement posture).
